column1: # Reinforcement that must stay attached to the rule it reinforces.
# COVERAGE.tsv pins rules. It cannot pin reinforcement — the sentences that make
# a rule actually fire. 51dfbcc: a compression pass kept every pinned phrase,
# dropped the clause explaining one of them, and measured behaviour broke while
# all 87 coverage rows still passed. These rows are that gap.
# Each row pins an anchor phrase plus the phrases that must appear in the SAME
# NEIGHBOURHOOD as the anchor. The neighbourhood is the containing paragraph: the
# block between blank lines. Not the whole file — a rewrite that guts a rule
# almost always leaves its words somewhere else in the document.
# Rule 0b — a pin retires on the same evidence that removes the text it pins.
# Rule 0 says pin before you cut, and pin inflation is Rule 0's own failure mode:
# pins already blanket ~70% of the output style, every compression phase adds
# more, and a ratchet with no downward pawl makes these two files the largest
# incompressible surface in the repository inside ten releases.
# So a row comes out only when (a) its provenance commit has been read and the
# documented failure it answers no longer reproduces under the Rule 1 pressure
# test, or (b) its upstream justification is documented as reversed — the pattern
# LIMITATIONS.md already records for the designer-temperature entry (c7690923).
# Same evidence to remove a pin as to cut pinned text. Never less.
# Matching is a case-folded FIXED SUBSTRING, not regex. Whitespace is normalised
# exactly as check-coverage.sh normalises it, so line-wrapped prose still
# matches. If the anchor appears more than once, the row passes when ANY one
# where          resolves as it does in COVERAGE.tsv: `output-styles`, an agent
# anchor         the pinned phrase; may already be pinned in COVERAGE.tsv.
# must_cooccur   `|`-separated, ALL required, never empty. An empty list asserts
#                nothing and is a broken row, not a passing one.
# Checked by scripts/check-reinforcement.sh. Exit 1 on any gutted rule.
